meta.label: AGENT-SIMULATED. Not human or real-learner data.
meta.method: One AI agent (Claude, run inside the build environment, no API key) role-played 9 learner runs (3 personas x 3 prior-knowledge levels) answering the 9 skills-check items in docs/skills-check/items.json, then reviewed each item. The same agent and model did both phases.
limitations: Single agent, single model: the persona answers and the item review come from the same model, so there is no independent second judge and no agreement figure.
The agent read items.json, including the answer key and feedback, before role-playing. Persona answers are a judgment of how such a learner would plausibly answer, not a blind attempt.
The agent may share a model family with the agent that wrote the items.
Nine runs cannot show learning gains or statistical significance.
meta.answer_letters: A, B, C follow the option order in items.json, which is also the on-screen order

item_review.reviewer: The same agent that produced the runs above (no independent second judge).

structural_checks.note: Deterministic checks on items.json and docs/skills-check/check.js; these do not depend on the simulation.
structural_checks.keyed_option_position: The keyed answer is option A in 9 of 9 items, and check.js renders options in file order (no shuffling).
structural_checks.keyed_option_longest: The keyed answer is the longest option in 7 of 9 items (all except p2 and p3).

items.issues: keyed option A contains the explanation (the extension talks to the app), which cues the answer; even no-prior runs chose it
items.notes: Move the explanation into the feedback and keep the option short.

items.issues: option C's own feedback says it can work, so two options are defensible for the stem as written
items.notes: Ask for the fastest fix that always works, or make C clearly worse.
Delete (B) drew the no-prior runs, which is the error the lesson targets.
The Word add-in store (B) drew runs with Mendeley experience, a realistic transfer error worth keeping as a distractor.
Corrupted data (B) drew novices; the item separates levels well.
Hand-typing the page (B) is the realistic mistake and drew the no-prior runs.

items.issues: keyed option A bundles three causes and is much longer than the distractors (122 characters vs 53 and 59)
items.notes: Shorten A to one cause or make the distractors equally specific.
Direct bibliography edit (B) drew 5 of 9 runs, the same error the item's feedback names from the support data.

items.issues: hardest item; 2 of 3 expert runs chose the open group (B)
items.notes: The difficulty comes from a real documented limitation that the group-libraries lesson already states, so the item is fair as written.
